daily_brief: The day's news was dominated by the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO following pressure from President Trump, a move that added nearly $1 trillion to the company's market value but drew criticism from lawmakers concerned about national security given Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy [BBC, Le Monde, Financial Times]. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte pledged to defend against threats in space after German intelligence reports indicated Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite dubbed 'Sputnik-S' within 60 days [BBC]. In China, Shanghai's powerful Communist Party Secretary Chen Jining was placed under investigation for 'severe violations of discipline and laws,' marking one of the highest-profile targets of Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign ahead of the 2027 Party Congress [The Hindu, Financial Times, Nikkei Asia]. Ukraine continued expanding its long-range strike capabilities, with President Zelenskyy confirming responsibility for drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libya and the Gulf of Finland, raising concerns among allies about escalation [The Guardian, ABC Australia]. Meanwhile, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Senegal won the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, ending an 11-month legal dispute with Morocco over the chaotic final [RFI].

top_stories.headline: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO After Trump Intervention, Adding $1 Trillion to Market Value
bullets: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO less than two weeks after resigning over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy
President Trump claimed he 'made the deal' with Nvidia's board to restore Huang, drawing backlash from lawmakers citing national security concerns
Nvidia shares jumped 31%, adding nearly $1 trillion to market value and boosting broader tech stocks
Huang faces Congressional testimony next week regarding his relationship with Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese intelligence operative

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on Trump's intervention and national security implications, included analysis of what the episode teaches China's Xi about Trump

top_stories.headline: NATO Pledges Space Defense as German Intelligence Reports Russia Preparing Nuclear Satellite Launch
bullets: German media reported intelligence indicates Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite dubbed 'Sputnik-S' within 60 days
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte stated the alliance will defend against any threats in space during a press conference with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
The satellite could reportedly be used to disrupt or destroy communication and observation satellites
Russia's Kremlin spokesman dismissed the reports as not worth taking seriously, calling them part of a 'propaganda campaign'

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting on NATO response and Russian denial

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Identical coverage to BBC World feed

top_stories.headline: Shanghai Communist Party Chief Chen Jining Placed Under Corruption Investigation
bullets: Chen Jining, 62, Shanghai's top Communist Party leader and Politburo member, was announced to be under investigation for 'suspected severe violations of discipline and laws'
Chen was widely expected to receive a prominent national role at the 2027 Party Congress where Xi Jinping is set to begin a fourth term
Chen previously served as president of Xi's alma mater Tsinghua University and as Beijing mayor before his Shanghai appointment in 2022
Politburo members are rarely investigated, with only half a dozen such cases historically

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Chen's international exposure including doctoral studies at Imperial College London

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.framing_note: Described Chen as caught up in Xi's anti-corruption campaign

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Claims Responsibility for Drone Strikes on Russian Ships in Libya and Gulf of Finland
bullets: Ukraine confirmed using seven naval drones launched from a mothership to strike two Russian vessels in Benghazi, Libya, sinking the corvette Merkury
President Zelenskyy also claimed responsibility for Saturday's drone strike on the cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland
The Libya operation occurred 1,500 miles from the frontline, representing a significant geographic expansion of Ukraine's strike capabilities
Russia called the attacks 'dangerous escalation' while Norway urged caution; Finland, Estonia and Russian vessels conducted joint rescue operations

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Detailed operational coverage, noted Ukraine developed sea drone capability despite starting war with no navy

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized escalation fears and allied concerns, noted Poland accused Russia of deliberately violating its airspace

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Analysis piece examining what strikes say about spread of Ukraine war

top_stories.headline: Court of Arbitration for Sport Declares Senegal 2025 Africa Cup of Nations Champions
bullets: CAS ruled in favor of Senegal, ending an 11-month legal dispute over the January 2026 final in which Senegal beat Morocco 1-0
Morocco had appealed after Senegalese players walked off the field without referee permission following a controversial penalty decision
CAF's appeals panel had initially sided with Morocco in March, declaring Senegal had forfeited by walking off
The ruling ends a saga that significantly damaged the reputation of Africa's most prestigious national team tournament

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive coverage of legal proceedings and tournament context
